analysis.title: Global Economics & Strategy Deep Speak: An AI-driven read on tone shifts at the Fed, ECB and BoJ
key_insights: UBS built an LLM-based tracker that scores policy-relevant remarks by the Fed, ECB and BoJ on a hawkish/dovish scale. It covers speeches, interviews and press conferences, is updated daily, spans more than two decades, and is available through a dashboard and a Python API.

Fed tone has risen steadily over recent months, and the slope of the climb now resembles 2022. Inflation is the largest driver and has mostly tracked headline PCE. Growth and labour tone have also firmed.
Fed hawkish momentum is broad-based across Board members and topics, not only inflation. Warsh and Jefferson lead the move. Q4 shows a more decisive hawkish shift across the Board.

ECB communication has continued to trend hawkish, but the aggregate signal swings more widely. Inflation is the dominant driver, but its impulse appears to have plateaued and inflation tone has stopped rising even as headline inflation is tracked.
ECB speaker-level hawkishness has normalised from the Q2-Q3 highs. Growth concerns partly offset inflation for some members, including Sleijpen and Elderson.

BoJ aggregate tone remains net hawkish but has shown little clear direction over the past year. Under the flat headline, inflation and rate guidance tone have slowly trended up, while growth and labour tone have held steady at hawkish levels.

BoJ board members are unusually aligned on the hawkish side in 2026, including Deputy Governor Uchida, who has historically been more dovish. Junko Koeda retains the clearest hawkish bias. The recent uptick in BoJ inflation tone tracks the pickup in headline and core inflation data.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The flat headline hides rising hawkishness in inflation and rate guidance, and board members are unusually aligned.
